pr_body:
# What does this PR do?

Fixes #30849. As it was reported in the issue, mamba was not using "use_cache" from generation kwargs. This PR adds it into kwargs and also returns the "cache_params", so that it can actually be used if `use_cache=True`

I tried to run Mamba test for generation locally, but it's failing for me even on `main` prob due to hardware differences (it has assertion on logits level)
pr_comments: The docs for this PR live [here](https://moon-ci-docs.huggingface.co/docs/transformers/pr_31116). All of your documentation changes will be reflected on that endpoint. The docs are available until 30 days after the last update.
Hope you don't mind the nits :D Just a mamba enthusiast over here.

Also tested the changes locally with commit a3cdff417bb3db94d5402dc009a07df97954a863 and it worked fine for `pytest tests/models/mamba -k "test_simple_generate" -s -vvvvv` (the logit levels test only). Haven't tried the others.

(GPU: 3080ti-16GB, CPU: 12th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-12700H)
Forgot to ask about benchmarking the generation speed btw, does it improve it (because now it's actually usingthe cache) ?
@ArthurZucker also forgot, will do a small evaluation to verify tomorrow :)
Out of curiosity, don't we have the same issue with Jamba?
@ylacombe hey! I just checked jamba and it seems to be passing the updated cache every step, so there should be no such problem. But let me know if you noticed something else :)

@ArthurZucker done! The evaluation shows that caching is faster and more memory efficient than without cache. Below are the results. no special setup and installations for mamba were done, I just tested in my usual transformer env.

Peak at: 27 MiB for cached generation
Time taken: 28.82830 s for cached generation

Peak at: 532 MiB for generation wo cache
Time taken: 829.49494 s for cached generation

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, MambaForCausalLM
import torch
from time import perf_counter

model_id = "state-spaces/mamba-2.8b-hf"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token
model = MambaForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto")
input_ids = tokenizer("Hey how are you doing?", return_tensors="pt")["input_ids"].to(model.device)

# Get init mem used up by model params
init_mem = torch.cuda.memory_allocated()
torch.cuda.reset_max_memory_allocated()

# Eval for cached generation
start = perf_counter()
out = model.generate(input_ids, do_sample=False, use_cache=True, max_new_tokens=500)
torch.cuda.synchronize()

total_time = perf_counter() - start
peak = (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - init_mem) // 1024 ** 2
print(f"Peak at: {peak} MiB for cached generation")
print(f"Time taken: {total_time:.05f} s for cached generation")

# Reset and start eval on use_cache=False
torch.cuda.reset_max_memory_allocated()

start = perf_counter()
out = model.generate(input_ids, do_sample=False, use_cache=False, max_new_tokens=500)
torch.cuda.synchronize()

total_time = perf_counter() - start
peak = (torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() - init_mem) // 1024 ** 2
print(f"Peak at: {peak} MiB for generation wo cache")
print(f"Time taken: {total_time:.05f} s for cached generation")
```

issue_context.title: Mamba: `use_cache` is not passed through in `prepare_inputs_for_generation`
issue_context.body:
Hi :)

I think that [use_cache](https://huggingface.co/docs/transformers/main/en/model_doc/mamba#transformers.MambaForCausalLM.forward.use_cache) is supposed to be passed through here as well:
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/9fd606dbdb392e76e66a4e4e852948ebf814dbb6/src/transformers/models/mamba/modeling_mamba.py#L634-L647

I noticed when I wanted to get the cache when using `model.generate`, but it was not there although I set `use_cache=True`.

Edit: Just saw that `GenerateDecoderOnlyOutput` would have to be adjusted as well. It would need to contain `cache_params` similarly to `past_key_values`. I don't know if it's okay for you to bloat that even more.
https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/blob/9fd606dbdb392e76e66a4e4e852948ebf814dbb6/src/transformers/generation/utils.py#L2244-L2251

Cheers and thanks for the great work!
comments: @zucchini-nlp could you have a look at this issue? 🤗

review_comments:
I removed `model.config.use_cache = True` just above this and moved it into the `generate`, to test that current changes are working and generate accepts "use_cache" in kwargs for Mamba. 

The real changes are the ones in `prepare_inputs_for_generation` which didn't pass `use_cache` in kwargs earlier
IMO we should not need to update the generation utils, unless we find cache params to be general enough?

We need to pass in updated "cache" into every forward call for the model to actually "use_cache". So we have to update `model_kwargs` in generation utils. CRIIW, as I am assuming from the code that Mamba caching works same as Transformer models

As you said below, if we don't want to follow XLNet style, I can use its own naming for cache. I think in that case we have to make changes in XLNet and other models with different cache names, to make generation utils consistent. Otherwise we'll be using forcefully `past_key_values` for several models except Mamba, thus adding unnecessary conditional checks
No, I think we ought to just leave previous model as is (they are using past_key_values) and just support arbitrary kwargs being returned from the model) / go with `cache_params`
